brief:
Work-related separation strains families everywhere, but in Gaza the burden falls with particular weight. We Are Not Numbers reports that fathers separated from their families by employment demands face acute emotional and practical hardship, with daughters often forced into roles beyond their years.

The absence reshapes household dynamics in a territory where economic pressure and limited opportunities already strain family structures. Children assume responsibilities their counterparts elsewhere might not encounter until adulthood, while parents contend with the dual pain of financial necessity and prolonged separation.
dek: Work-related separation is not uncommon. In Gaza, the ache of absence is more acute.
title: Gaza father's work separation deepens family strain
